title: Match Key
description: One identifier a party can resolve, the entity scopes it resolves at, and the uses it supports. Capability only: MUST NOT carry match rates, audience sizes, coverage, or per-user or per-graph data. Two keys are compatible at scope S when they share uid_type, both list S in scopes, their vendor domains are equal when both declare vendor, and they declare the same scope_resolution (absent means graph). Sellers using this shape list media_buy.match_keys in experimental_features.

uid_type.description: Identifier type. Match keys draw from uid-type only; supported_identifier_types is not a match-key source.

vendor.description: Party that forms the entity at the declared scopes: the graph or resolution vendor, or the seller itself when it forms the entity (scope_resolution serve_time, or a graph the seller runs). Names who forms the entity, not who supplied input data such as an IP or device-signal feed. Required when uid_type is other, when scopes include households, and when a maid or publisher_first_party key lists individuals: the party that forms those entities is named.

scopes.description: Entity granularities this key resolves at; list each when there are several. custom is not comparable across parties and is excluded.

enumDescriptions.graph: A persistent graph, licensed or run by the seller and named in vendor, resolves the key to the declared scopes. The grouping is stable between requests, apart from graph refreshes.
enumDescriptions.serve_time: The seller groups the key into the declared scopes at request time from network and device signals, for example IP address and user agent, without a persistent graph. vendor is the seller's own domain. The grouping can change between requests as addresses are reassigned or devices move between networks.

scope_resolution.description: How the key reaches its non-native scopes (households, or individuals for maid and publisher_first_party). Absent means graph, so existing declarations keep their meaning. A key with serve_time is compatible only with keys that also declare serve_time and the same vendor, which in practice means the same forming party, usually one seller: two sellers that each group by IP form different households for the same home.

uses.description: Purposes this key supports at the declared scopes.

property_types.description: Seller-wide declarations only: property types on which this key resolves. Omit to mean every property type the seller sells. Product-level keys inherit the product's property types.

allOf.description: A key outside the uid-type enum is identified by its vendor.
Household resolution always names the party that forms the household: a graph vendor, or the seller when scope_resolution is serve_time.
A device or publisher identifier reaches a person only through a graph.
PAIR is publisher-scoped and rotates every 30 days, and unsalted hashed_email in TMP widens the identity-leak surface until #8449 is resolved, so neither is forwarded to buyer-side Identity Match.
